subject: Commit ladder proposal, token ledger, and latency evidence for renewal
messages:
From: Sasha Reed <sasha@novex.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@novex.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal prep: sudden token spike + latency notes

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this early look. We went digging into Q3 usage and saw a ~38% token surge in the past six weeks tied to a new inference pipeline we rolled out. Coupled with that, our app team is seeing intermittent 95th percentile latency regressions (~350ms -> ~520ms) on text-generation calls.

We have our renewal in late September and need to understand whether the current commit still makes sense or if we should layer a staged bump + burst credits. Can your team share a short ledger of token spend by model, and any latency sample evidence you have? Also, we need an initial view of the incremental unit economics if we were to step up committed capacity by 20%.

I attached the raw billing extract we exported and flagged the high-variance days. Priya (procurement) is on copy to start the contract path if we agree a change.

Goals for this week: a short meeting to align on the usage drivers and a proposed amendment that preserves Novex pricing tiers if we increase commit.

Thanks,
Sasha
Sasha Reed
Head of ML Platform, Novex.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Reed <sasha@novex.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep: sudden token spike + latency notes

Sasha, thanks for the ledger. Quick summary from our side after a first pass:

- Token drivers: 1) a higher request rate to the aligner model (aligner-v1) after the new pipeline, 2) longer avg prompt lengths on batch inference for personalization (up ~18%).
- Latency: the 95th regressions line up with two microcode rollouts we had in early August and a transient memory pressure event on the dedicated pool that hit a subset of requests. We	attached a short sample PDF (latency-sample-0801-0814.pdf) showing the correlation.
- Econ: stepping commit up by 20% reduces unit token cost by ~12% on our pricing ladder and gives you predictable burst capacity; however, it requires an amendment to the term.

Attached: novex-usage-q3.csv (cleaned), latency-sample-0801-0814.pdf. I think a staged "commit ladder" makes sense: +10% now with a 30-day review and option to add the remaining +10% at 60 days if throughput stabilizes. We can protect you with a one-time burst credit for the immediate spike and keep the original tier pricing for the added commit.

Proposed next steps (short):
- 30-minute alignment call (I	created a tentative slot tomorrow 11am PT)
- If we agree, I will route a draft amendment with the commit ladder and the burst credit to Sales Ops and legal.

If that sounds OK I	ll loop in Ben for the promotional credit approval and Marissa for renewal coordination.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Aug 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal prep: sudden token spike + latency notes

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Fwding Novex thread. TL;DR: customer hit a ~38% token spike; proposing a two-step commit ladder (+10% now, +10% at 60 days) + a one-time burst credit to smooth immediate overages. They want to keep current tier pricing for any added committed capacity.

Ask: can Sales Ops make the amendment draft with the ladder language and a one-time 50k token burst credit? Ben - can you sign off on the credit and any standard concessions? Marissa - can we get this into your renewal tracker and confirm the DocuSign flow?

Attached are the usage CSV and the latency PDF I sent to them. I	think we should keep the ask modest and staged to minimize revenue friction but preserve goodwill.

Thanks,
Evelyn

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Aug 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal prep: sudden token spike + latency notes

Eve	— approved the 50k token burst credit as a one-time concession. Sales Ops: please draft amendment with commit ladder language and include an option to revert the second step if usage drops by >20% during the 60-day window. Keep the pricing tier intact.

-Ben

From: Sasha Reed <sasha@novex.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@novex.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep: sudden token spike + latency notes

Thanks, Evelyn and team. The ladder model and one-time burst credit sound workable. Two asks from our side before we sign:

1) Can we get the amendment to reflect an SLA credit if the 95th pct latency remains >450ms for more than 72 hours in aggregate during the 60-day review window?
2) Can the amendment list which model variants are in scope for the committed unit economics (aligner-v1, generator-v3-small)? We want to avoid surprises if you change the served variant.

If you can include those lines, Priya will route to procurement and we can execute quickly. Also, thanks for the latency sample—it helped us correlate to our orchestration windows.

Best,
Sasha

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Reed <sasha@novex.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Aug 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep: sudden token spike + latency notes

Sasha / Priya —

Appreciate the clarity. We will: 1) add an SLA credit clause (if aggregate 95th pct >450ms for >72h during the 60-day window, customer eligible for pro-rated service credit), and 2) enumerate in-scope model variants (aligner-v1 and generator-v3-small) for the economics.

I	attached a draft amendment (amendment-draft-v2.docx) and placed the DocuSign link in the related links. Marissa — can you confirm the renewal tracker entry and the DocuSign envelope ID? Ben — thanks for the credit approval.

Next steps:
- We	will push the amendment to DocuSign by end of day Monday.
- Tentative 30-day check-in scheduled for Sept 18 to verify the ladder and post-step performance.

If there	are no further asks I	ll route the DocuSign and mark this as renewal-in-flight.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
